# I: Headless Blender code-modelling PoC (Cyrus L4 route a)

Run 2026-10-10 on node-2, workspace `/tank/nxeon-build/tmp/blender-poc/`. One agent, no sub-agents, no paid APIs. Sources in `blender-poc/src/` (harness.py, sbx.sh logic, prop scripts per round). Renders and glbs in `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-research/blender-poc/` (glbs in `out/`).

## Setup (VERIFIED)
- Blender **5.2.2 LTS** (current LTS per blender.org/download/lts) portable tarball, sha256 `84098912...a168` matched the file published at download.blender.org. Never installed system-wide.
- Run only as `blender --background --factory-startup --python harness.py -- prop.py name`.
- Sandbox: a transient systemd unit in `nxeon-build-agents.slice` holding the node-2 build lock (same properties as run-capped.sh plus extras). I called systemd-run directly because `devhost` insists on a git worktree of the repo, which would have changed the repo.
- Extras: `PrivateNetwork=yes` (no network), User=nobody, `ProtectSystem=strict`, `/opt /tank /var/lib /mnt` replaced by empty tmpfs apart from the Blender dir (read-only) and a work dir, MemoryMax 4G, CPUQuota 400%, TasksMax 256, RuntimeMax, no capabilities, NoNewPrivileges.
- Renderer: Cycles CPU, 32 spp, denoise, 640x480 (crate) / 768x480 (rifle), 3 views + contact sheet. EEVEE not tried (no GPU). Three.js/Playwright render of the glb: **not done (UNVERIFIED)**; glb checked via Blender re-import and Khronos gltf-validator instead.
- Harness prelude (`mat`, `box`, `cyl`, `prism`, join-by-material, smart_project, export, render) is fixed code I wrote once. It is effectively a tiny parts kit, so per-prop scripts are shorter than a cold start would be.

## Results per prop
| | Crate (A) | Rifle (B) |
|---|---|---|
| Rounds used | 3 of 6 | 4 of 6 |
| Wall per round | 26-28 s (render ~21 s inside Blender, rest ssh/scp) | 26 s |
| Triangles (final) | 6,720 | 2,732 |
| Objects after join by material | 5 (64 before) | 3 |
| Per-object non-manifold edges (bmesh) | 0 | 0 |
| UV present | yes, all objects (smart_project) | yes |
| glb valid | validator: 0 errors, 0 warnings; Blender re-import tri count equal | same |
| glb size | 476 KB | 187 KB |
| Quality vs intent | **7.5/10** | **6.5/10** |
| Est. tokens | ~15k (UNVERIFIED, from session counter) | ~20k |

Quality is my own judgement from the renders. The crate reads as a sci-fi supply crate: panels, ribs, chunky corner caps, latches, end handles, glowing strip. The rifle is recognisably AK-pattern in side, 3/4 and top views: curved magazine, slanted grip, gas tube, wood furniture, muzzle brake, front sight. It looks stylised-blocky and flat-shaded with no wear or textures.

## Round log (renders: `<prop>-r<N>-<3q|side|back|top>.png`, sheet `<prop>-r<N>-sheet.png`)
| Round | What changed |
|---|---|
| crate-r1 | First script. Pale and overexposed; read as a filing cabinet; glow strip hidden behind a panel. |
| crate-r2 | Darker palette, chunky corner caps, ribbed panels, yellow label, glow moved in front of the panel, handles moved up. Reads as a crate. |
| crate-r3 (final) | Darker lid, saturated glow, lid ribs, join by material, exposure -0.9. (The exposure change reached node-2 only for r3; r1 and r2 were rendered at exposure 0 because my sync script forgot harness.py.) |
| rifle-r1 | First script. Already recognisable; mag thin, wood pale, trigger guard a full ring. |
| rifle-r2 | Darker wood, U-shaped trigger guard, fatter mag and grip, butt plate, trunnion. |
| rifle-r3 | Added cover ribs and handguard grooves. The cover ribs looked like a rail comb (a regression). |
| rifle-r4 (final) | Removed cover ribs, kept grooves. |
Final sheets: `crate-final-sheet.png`, `rifle-final-sheet.png`.

## What failed or was weak (VERIFIED from renders)
- First attempts have wrong proportions, colours and exposure. Most gains came from looking at the picture (hidden glow strip, regression from the cover ribs); the numeric checks alone caught none of them.
- "Manifold" is per closed shell. Parts overlap and are not boolean-unioned, so the mesh is not one watertight solid. Interior faces are wasted triangles.
- Rifle details are cuboid and cylinder primitives. Organic curves (stock, grip) are crude. Texturing is flat colours only; no normal bake or LOD was attempted.
- 1 m scale holds (bbox 1.03 m rifle; crate 1.14 x 0.70 x 0.65 m including handles and feet).

## Safety (sandbox probes VERIFIED)
A model-written script runs full Python inside Blender: `os`, `subprocess`, `socket`, file access, `bpy.ops.wm.url_open`.
| Probe | Result in sandbox |
|---|---|
| connect to 1.1.1.1, DNS, curl subprocess | blocked (no network namespace) |
| read /root, /etc/shadow, other pids' environ | permission denied |
| list /opt, /etc/nxeon-build, /var/lib, /home | empty |
| write /etc, /usr, /tank | read-only filesystem |
| write to work dir; run `id` | allowed; uid 65534 |
| `while True`, 100 MB allocation loop, fork bomb | killed at the timeout; killed by OOM in 4 s; contained by TasksMax and timeout. No units left behind. |
Not verified: kernel-exploit escapes (a systemd unit is not a VM). The real worker needs a stronger boundary (gVisor, microVM, or an allow-list that rejects `import os/subprocess/socket` before running) plus the same no-network and cap properties. Pre-run static rejection and the sandbox should both be used.

## Cost
About 5k tokens per round (script 1.5-2.5k output, image read ~2k, stats 0.5k), 3-4 rounds, so roughly 15-20k tokens per finished prop here with a fixed prelude. A cold start without the prelude, or props 3-5x more complex, would be higher; I did not measure that. Compute is about 25 s of 4 CPU threads per round. A customer price must cover: tokens x rounds (and retries that end in rejection), CPU seconds, human fix time, and the risk of failed or rejected jobs. I cannot back a dollar figure without current token pricing and failure rates.

## Recommendation
- **GO for the code-modelling route for stylised hard-surface props** (crates, lanterns, simplified guns) as a "draft for a human to fix". Not a GO for hero or realistic assets, organic shapes, or likeness.
- A **parts kit** (bevelled box, panel, handle, cylinder, curved-profile prism, join and UV, material presets, camera and light rig) would cut tokens per round, lock scale and conventions, and make failures less likely. Add a union-then-cleanup pass so the output is closer to one watertight mesh.
- Measure next: (1) 20+ varied prompts, success rate at <=4 rounds, tokens per success; (2) a vision-model "look" step instead of me, and how often it catches regressions like rifle-r3; (3) boolean union, decimate to `meshBudget`, LOD and bake time; (4) in-engine load (three.js/FiveM) and texture quality; (5) the stronger sandbox; (6) a blind rating of "not cheap" by the owner.
# K: Parametric template + parts kit PoC (Cyrus L4, follow-up to I-blender-poc.md)

2026-10-10, node-2, same sandbox as PoC 1 (Blender 5.2.2, systemd-run, no network, user nobody, read-only fs, build lock). No sub-agents, no paid APIs, no repo touched. Files: `blender-poc/partkit/` (renders `<prompt>-r<N>-{side,3q,top,sheet}.png`, `<prompt>-final-sheet.png`, glbs in `out/`, sources in `src/`).

## What was built (VERIFIED, runs)
- `pk_geo.py` closed bmesh primitives (box/cylinder/rod/prism), bevel, per-face material slots, smooth+sharp-edge shading.
- `pk_parts.py` parts kit: 4 receivers (ak_stamped, modern_slab, smg_boxy, bullpup_shell), 4 grips, 3 magazines (curved, straight_box, drum), 6 stocks (fixed_wood, fixed_poly, folding_wire, folding_strut, bullpup_integral, none), 5 handguards (wood_ak, rail_quad, slim_poly, ribbed_shroud, none), 4 barrel profiles, 4 muzzle devices, gas tube, 4 sight types, 6 glow-strip placements, 7 palette slots.
- `pk_rifle.py` template: JSON spec in, 7-8 named objects out (receiver, grip, magazine, stock, handguard, barrel, sights, trim), UVs via smart_project, glb. Bad enum values raise an error naming the allowed values. Untested variants: drum, rail_quad, modern_slab, folding_strut, folded stock, fixed_poly.
- 439 lines / 28 KB. The model-facing "spec card" is 960 chars (about 300 tokens, cacheable).

## Results (3 prompts, 2 rounds each, only the JSON changed)
| | AK-style | Bullpup sci-fi + glow | SMG, folding stock |
|---|---|---|---|
| JSON size per round | 340 / 430 B (~110-140 tok) | 520 / 570 B | 430 / 470 B |
| Rounds | 2 | 2 | 2 |
| Tokens, session counter delta (my output + tool results, incl. my reasoning) | 3.0k | 5.8k (1.5k lost to a tool timeout) | 5.2k |
| + image reads (est. 1.1k per sheet, UNVERIFIED) | +2.2k | +2.2k | +2.2k |
| Total est. | ~5.2k | ~8.0k | ~7.4k |
| Lean est. (JSON 150 + card 300 cached + stats 350 + image 1.1k per round) | ~3.8k | ~3.8k | ~3.8k |
| Wall | ~28 s per round (23 s Cycles render; geometry under 1 s) | same | same |
| Tris | 1,452 | 948 | 1,412 |
| Non-manifold edges (per object) | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| UV on all objects | yes (7/7) | yes (8/8) | yes (7/7) |
| glTF validator | 0 errors, 0 warnings | 0/0 | 0/0 |
| Quality vs intent (my judgement from renders) | **7/10** | **6.5/10** | **7/10** |

PoC 1 AK for comparison: 6.5/10, 4 rounds, ~15-20k tokens, 2,732 tris.

Adjustments made after looking: AK r1 to r2 fixed a near-black receiver that hid detail (palette) and tapered the barrel. Bullpup r1 to r2 fixed a plain white slab (palette), added more glow strips. SMG r1 to r2 fixed monochrome low contrast. All three fixes were palette or minor parameters. None changed the silhouette.

Mesh caveat (VERIFIED): "manifold" is per closed shell. Primitives overlap and are not unioned (bullpup receiver has 18 shells, AK barrel 6), same as PoC 1. All three are under 10k tris (6-15% of budget), so there is room for more detail.

## What the template could NOT express
Contoured bullpup stock/cheek weld (stock is a slab plus pad); sight position and optic/rail layout (fixed anchors, red dot reads as a block); organic grips and ergonomics; folded-stock state was not tested; wear, damage, normal maps and textures (flat colours only); any non-rifle class (pistol, shotgun, bolt-action, belt-fed, launcher); underbarrel, bipod, light, scope; per-part offsets; asymmetric left/right features.

## Cost and break-even
| | Tokens | Time |
|---|---|---|
| One-time template + kit build (counter, 68.7k total incl. ~6k reading PoC 1; ~60k net) | ~60-65k | ~10 min agent wall (16:39 to 16:48, 3 sandbox runs for bug fixes); a human would need roughly 4-6 h (UNVERIFIED) |
| From scratch per rifle (PoC 1, fixed prelude) | 15-20k | 4 rounds |
| Template per rifle, measured | 5-8k | 2 rounds |
| Saving per prompt | ~10-14k measured, ~12-16k on lean est. | |

Break-even is about **5-6 prompts** if every prompt fits the template (60k / ~11k), about 4 on the lean estimate, and about **10-12 prompts at a 50% fit rate** (misfits fall back to the next rung). Each new object class (pistol, vehicle, crate) needs its own template; I would guess 30-40k for the second (geo layer reused, UNVERIFIED).

## Verdict on the hypothesis
- Token cut: **2.5-3x measured, about 5x on the lean estimate**. The 5-10x target is not reached or proven. One-round success would approach 8-10x (about 2k) but this PoC never got a one-round pass: first JSONs were all palette-weak.
- Quality: equal or slightly better (7 / 6.5 / 7 vs 6.5), more consistent scale, UVs and part names by construction.
- Risk removed: the model emits data only, no executable code, so the static-rejection problem from PoC 1 largely disappears for this rung (UNVERIFIED in a real worker).
- Next: a vision step that picks palette automatically (the only fix needed every time); let the parts kit take part offsets in JSON; measure template-fit rate over 20+ real prompts; try parts-kit assembly rung (model writes a list of part calls) for misfits.

#!/bin/bash
# usage: pk_run.sh SPEC.json NAME(e.g. smg-r1)  -> sync, run in sandbox, pull side/3q/top + sheet + glb
set -e
D=/root/agent-notes/cyrus-research/blender-poc/partkit; H=root@178.63.94.114; W=/tank/nxeon-build/tmp/blender-poc
scp -q $D/src/pk_*.py $D/src/$1 $H:$W/in/ && ssh $H "chmod 644 $W/in/*"
s=$(date +%s); b=${2//-/_}
ssh $H "cd $W && ./sbx.sh pk_harness.py -- $1 $b 2>&1 | grep -E 'STATS_JSON|Error|error|Traceback|File |line [0-9]|Exception' | head -30"
echo "wall_s=$(( $(date +%s) - s ))"
i=0; for v in side 3q top; do scp -q $H:$W/work/${b}_v$i.png $D/$2-$v.png || true; i=$((i+1)); done
scp -q $H:$W/work/${b}_sheet.png $D/$2-sheet.png || true
mkdir -p $D/out; scp -q $H:$W/work/$b.glb $D/out/$2.glb || true
# pk_harness.py -- fixed infra (written once): blender -b --python pk_harness.py -- spec.json NAME
import bpy, bmesh, sys, os, math, time, json
import numpy as np
from mathutils import Vector
sys.dont_write_bytecode = True
IN = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)); sys.path.insert(0, IN)
SPEC, NAME = sys.argv[sys.argv.index('--') + 1:][:2]
OUT = os.getcwd(); t0 = time.time()
bpy.ops.object.select_all(action='SELECT'); bpy.ops.object.delete()
for blk in (bpy.data.meshes, bpy.data.materials, bpy.data.lights, bpy.data.cameras):
    for b in list(blk): blk.remove(b)
import pk_rifle
spec = json.load(open(os.path.join(IN, SPEC)))
objs, A = pk_rifle.build(spec)
RES = (768, 480)
for o in objs:   # UVs
    bpy.ops.object.select_all(action='DESELECT'); o.select_set(True); bpy.context.view_layer.objects.active = o
    bpy.ops.object.mode_set(mode='EDIT'); bpy.ops.mesh.select_all(action='SELECT')
    bpy.ops.uv.smart_project(angle_limit=math.radians(66), island_margin=0.02); bpy.ops.object.mode_set(mode='OBJECT')
t_build = time.time() - t0
stats = dict(objects=len(objs), tris=0, nonmanifold_edges=0, uv_objs=0, per_obj={}); lo = Vector((1e9,) * 3); hi = Vector((-1e9,) * 3)
for o in objs:
    bm = bmesh.new(); bm.from_mesh(o.data)
    tris = sum(len(f.verts) - 2 for f in bm.faces); nm = sum(1 for e in bm.edges if not e.is_manifold)
    # shells = connected components (overlapping primitives are NOT unioned)
    seen = set(); shells = 0
    for v in bm.verts:
        if v.index in seen: continue
        shells += 1; st = [v]; seen.add(v.index)
        while st:
            c = st.pop()
            for e in c.link_edges:
                w = e.other_vert(c)
                if w.index not in seen: seen.add(w.index); st.append(w)
    stats['tris'] += tris; stats['nonmanifold_edges'] += nm; stats['uv_objs'] += bool(o.data.uv_layers)
    for v in bm.verts:
        for i in range(3): lo[i] = min(lo[i], v.co[i]); hi[i] = max(hi[i], v.co[i])
    stats['per_obj'][o.name] = (tris, nm, shells); bm.free()
stats['bbox_m'] = [round(hi[i] - lo[i], 3) for i in range(3)]
glb = os.path.join(OUT, NAME + '.glb')
bpy.ops.export_scene.gltf(filepath=glb, export_format='GLB', export_apply=True, export_yup=True)
stats['glb_bytes'] = os.path.getsize(glb)
center = (lo + hi) / 2; size = max(hi - lo); sc = bpy.context.scene
sc.render.engine = 'CYCLES'; sc.cycles.device = 'CPU'; sc.cycles.samples = 32; sc.cycles.use_denoising = True
sc.render.resolution_x, sc.render.resolution_y = RES
w = bpy.data.worlds.new('w'); sc.world = w; w.use_nodes = True
bg = w.node_tree.nodes['Background']; bg.inputs[0].default_value = (0.32, 0.34, 0.38, 1); bg.inputs[1].default_value = 1.0
sc.view_settings.view_transform = 'AgX'; sc.view_settings.exposure = -0.9
bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_plane_add(size=size * 8, location=(center.x, center.y, lo.z - 0.002))
gp = bpy.context.active_object; gm = bpy.data.materials.new('_g'); gm.use_nodes = True
gm.node_tree.nodes['Principled BSDF'].inputs['Base Color'].default_value = (0.22, 0.22, 0.24, 1); gm.node_tree.nodes['Principled BSDF'].inputs['Roughness'].default_value = 0.9; gp.data.materials.append(gm)
def light(loc, energy, size_):
    d = bpy.data.lights.new('l', 'AREA'); d.energy = energy; d.size = size_
    o = bpy.data.objects.new('l', d); bpy.context.collection.objects.link(o); o.location = loc
    c = o.constraints.new('TRACK_TO'); t = bpy.data.objects.new('t', None); bpy.context.collection.objects.link(t); t.location = center
    c.target = t; c.track_axis = 'TRACK_NEGATIVE_Z'; c.up_axis = 'UP_Y'
R = size * 3
light(center + Vector((R, -R, R * 1.2)), 900 * size * size + 300, size * 3)
light(center + Vector((-R, -R * .5, R * .6)), 300 * size * size + 100, size * 3)
light(center + Vector((0, R, R * .8)), 400 * size * size + 100, size * 3)

# pk_geo.py -- low-level geometry kit: closed bmesh primitives accumulated into named Parts, material slots per face.
import bpy, bmesh, math
from mathutils import Matrix, Vector, Euler

SLOTS = ['body', 'furniture', 'barrel', 'mag', 'accent', 'glow', 'dark']
SIDX = {s: i for i, s in enumerate(SLOTS)}
DEFAULT_PAL = {  # slot: (hex, metallic, roughness, emission strength)
    'body': ('#3a3d42', 0.8, 0.40, 0), 'furniture': ('#6b3a1c', 0.0, 0.5, 0), 'barrel': ('#1c1e21', 0.9, 0.35, 0),
    'mag': ('#16181b', 0.6, 0.45, 0), 'accent': ('#8a8f98', 0.5, 0.4, 0), 'glow': ('#00e5ff', 0.0, 0.3, 6.0),
    'dark': ('#0b0c0e', 0.2, 0.7, 0)}

def hex2lin(h):
    h = h.lstrip('#'); return tuple((int(h[i:i + 2], 16) / 255.0) ** 2.2 for i in (0, 2, 4))

def make_materials(pal):
    mats = []
    for s in SLOTS:
        d = DEFAULT_PAL[s]; hx, me, ro, em = d
        v = (pal or {}).get(s)
        if isinstance(v, str): hx = v
        elif isinstance(v, dict):
            hx = v.get('color', hx); me = v.get('metal', me); ro = v.get('rough', ro); em = v.get('emit', em)
        m = bpy.data.materials.new('mat_' + s); m.use_nodes = True
        b = m.node_tree.nodes['Principled BSDF']; c = hex2lin(hx)
        b.inputs['Base Color'].default_value = (*c, 1); b.inputs['Metallic'].default_value = me; b.inputs['Roughness'].default_value = ro
        if em:
            b.inputs['Emission Color'].default_value = (*c, 1); b.inputs['Emission Strength'].default_value = em
        mats.append(m)
    return mats

def _bevel(bm, w, ang=35):
    if w <= 0: return
    es = [e for e in bm.edges if len(e.link_faces) == 2 and e.calc_face_angle(0) > math.radians(ang)]
    if es: bmesh.ops.bevel(bm, geom=es, offset=w, segments=1, profile=0.5, affect='EDGES', clamp_overlap=True)

def _M(loc, rot):
    return Matrix.Translation(loc) @ Euler(rot, "XYZ").to_matrix().to_4x4()

class Part:
    def __init__(self, name):
        self.name = name; self.bm = bmesh.new()
    def _add(self, src, slot, M=None):
        bmesh.ops.recalc_face_normals(src, faces=src.faces)
        if M is not None: bmesh.ops.transform(src, matrix=M, verts=src.verts)
        vm = {v: self.bm.verts.new(v.co) for v in src.verts}; idx = SIDX[slot]
        for f in src.faces:
            nf = self.bm.faces.new([vm[v] for v in f.verts]); nf.material_index = idx
        src.free()
    def box(self, c, dim, slot, bevel=0.0, rot=(0, 0, 0)):
        bm = bmesh.new(); bmesh.ops.create_cube(bm, size=1.0)
        bmesh.ops.scale(bm, vec=Vector(dim), verts=bm.verts)
        _bevel(bm, min(bevel, min(dim) * 0.3)); self._add(bm, slot, _M(c, rot))
    def cyl(self, c, r, length, slot, axis='x', r2=None, seg=16, bevel=0.0, rot=(0, 0, 0)):
        bm = bmesh.new()
        bmesh.ops.create_cone(bm, cap_ends=True, cap_tris=False, segments=seg, radius1=r, radius2=r if r2 is None else r2, depth=length, calc_uvs=False)
        _bevel(bm, min(bevel, r * 0.5, length * 0.3))
        base = {'x': Matrix.Rotation(math.pi / 2, 4, 'Y'), 'y': Matrix.Rotation(-math.pi / 2, 4, 'X'), 'z': Matrix.Identity(4)}[axis]
        self._add(bm, slot, _M(c, rot) @ base)
    def rod(self, p0, p1, r, slot, seg=8):
        p0 = Vector(p0); p1 = Vector(p1); d = p1 - p0
        bm = bmesh.new()
        bmesh.ops.create_cone(bm, cap_ends=True, cap_tris=False, segments=seg, radius1=r, radius2=r, depth=d.length, calc_uvs=False)
        q = Vector((0, 0, 1)).rotation_difference(d.normalized())
        self._add(bm, slot, Matrix.Translation((p0 + p1) / 2) @ q.to_matrix().to_4x4())
    def prism(self, pts, w, slot, bevel=0.0, plane='xz', c=0.0):
        """plane 'xz': pts=(x,z), extruded across y by w centred on y=c.  plane 'yz': pts=(y,z), extruded along x from c to c+w."""
        bm = bmesh.new(); n = len(pts)
        if plane == 'xz':
            a = [bm.verts.new((x, c - w / 2, z)) for x, z in pts]; b = [bm.verts.new((x, c + w / 2, z)) for x, z in pts]
        else:
            a = [bm.verts.new((c, y, z)) for y, z in pts]; b = [bm.verts.new((c + w, y, z)) for y, z in pts]
        bm.faces.new(a); bm.faces.new(b[::-1])
        for i in range(n):
            j = (i + 1) % n; bm.faces.new((a[i], a[j], b[j], b[i]))
        _bevel(bm, min(bevel, w * 0.3)); self._add(bm, slot)
    def to_object(self, mats, sharp_deg=35):
        bm = self.bm
        bmesh.ops.recalc_face_normals(bm, faces=bm.faces)
        for f in bm.faces: f.smooth = True
        for e in bm.edges:
            if len(e.link_faces) != 2 or e.calc_face_angle(0) > math.radians(sharp_deg): e.smooth = False
        me = bpy.data.meshes.new(self.name); bm.to_mesh(me); bm.free()
        for m in mats: me.materials.append(m)
        ob = bpy.data.objects.new(self.name, me); bpy.context.collection.objects.link(ob)
        return ob
# pk_rifle.py -- PARAMETRIC RIFLE TEMPLATE. build(spec_dict) -> (list of bpy objects, info). The AI step only emits `spec`.
import math, bpy
from pk_geo import Part, make_materials
from pk_parts import RECV, GRIP, MAG, STOCK, HAND, barrel, sights, trigger_guard, g

PART_NAMES = ['receiver', 'grip', 'magazine', 'stock', 'handguard', 'barrel', 'sights', 'trim']
def pick(table, S, key, default):
    st = (S or {}).get('style', default)
    if st not in table: raise ValueError(f'{key}.style={st!r} not in {sorted(table)}')
    return table[st]

def accents(P, A, lst, glow='glow'):
    T = P['trim']; w = A['w']
    for a in lst or []:
        if a == 'receiver_side':
            for s in (-1, 1): T.box(((A['x0'] + A['x1']) / 2 + 0.02, s * (w / 2 + 0.0008), A['zmid'] + 0.012), ((A['x1'] - A['x0']) * 0.5, 0.0016, 0.006), glow)
        elif a == 'receiver_top':
            T.box(((A['x0'] + A['x1']) / 2, 0, A['z_top'] + 0.0006), ((A['x1'] - A['x0']) * 0.6, 0.006, 0.0016), glow)
        elif a == 'handguard_side':
            for s in (-1, 1): T.box(((A['hg_x0'] + A['hg_x1']) / 2 + 0.01, s * (A['hg_w'] + 0.0006), A['hg_zmid'] + 0.002), (A['hg_x1'] - A['hg_x0'] - 0.06, 0.0016, 0.006), glow)
        elif a == 'magazine_window' and 'mag_mid' in A:
            x, z, rot, mw = A['mag_mid']
            for s in (-1, 1): T.box((x, s * (mw / 2 + 0.0006), z), (0.008, 0.0016, 0.07), glow, rot=(0, rot, 0))
        elif a == 'stock_side' and A.get('stock_len', 0) > 0:
            for s in (-1, 1): T.box((-A['stock_len'] * 0.5, s * 0.0215, 0.0), (A['stock_len'] * 0.5, 0.0016, 0.006), glow)
        elif a == 'barrel_ring':
            T.cyl((A['muzzle_x'] - 0.03, 0, 0), g(A.get('_b'), 'radius', 0.0115) * 1.5, 0.006, glow, seg=16)
        else: raise ValueError(f'accent {a!r} unknown/unavailable')

def build(spec):
    P = {n: Part(n) for n in PART_NAMES}; A = {}
    pick(RECV, spec.get('receiver'), 'receiver', 'ak_stamped')(P, spec.get('receiver', {}), A)
    GS = spec.get('grip', {}); pick(GRIP, GS, 'grip', 'ak_slanted')(P, GS, A)
    if GS.get('style') != 'none' and spec.get('trigger_guard', True): trigger_guard(P, GS, A)
    MS = spec.get('magazine', {}); pick(MAG, MS, 'magazine', 'curved')(P, MS, A)
    SS = spec.get('stock', {}); pick(STOCK, SS, 'stock', 'fixed_wood')(P, SS, A)
    HS = spec.get('handguard', {}); pick(HAND, HS, 'handguard', 'wood_ak')(P, HS, A)
    BS = spec.get('barrel', {}); A['_b'] = BS
    if 'hg_x0' in HS: pass
    barrel(P, BS, A, bool(spec.get('gas_tube', False)))
    sights(P, spec.get('sights', {}), A, g(BS, 'radius', 0.0115))
    accents(P, A, spec.get('accents'))
    mats = make_materials(spec.get('palette'))
    objs = []
    for n in PART_NAMES:
        if len(P[n].bm.faces): objs.append(P[n].to_object(mats))
        else: P[n].bm.free()
    return objs, A

# Cyrus Model Studio: plan (design only, 2026-10-10)

Labels: **V** = I read it in code (cyrus-r2 `lib/cyrus`, cyrus-r13 `assets3d/manifest.ts`, `adapters/asset-profile.ts`, `jobs/asset-jobs.ts`). **U** = unverified. Every quality claim about AI output is **U until a paid eval runs**. Mockups: `*.html` + `shots/` in this folder.

## 1. What exists today (V)
| Piece | Where | Fact that matters here |
|---|---|---|
| RigSpec v1 | `creature/spec.ts` | Zod `strictObject`; bones/cubes/clips; caps 32 bones, 64 cubes, 8 clips, 48 KB; model never writes UVs |
| Compiler | `creature/compile.ts` | box UV `boxFaces` + shelf `layoutSkin` (64/128), deterministic `.bbmodel` (rig-c1) |
| Preview | `creature/preview.ts` | pure software rasteriser, byte-stable PNG |
| Item states | `itemmodel/*` | 8 display contexts, per-category transforms, states; gun transform U in client |
| Texture Studio | `studios/paint.ts`, `editor.ts`, `service.ts` | `TextureDoc` = locked spec + sparse paint layer; `History<T>` 200 steps; save = new revision + asset row, `expectedHeadId` → 409 `stale_head` |
| Gate | `engine-core/asset-gate.ts` | `ASSET_MIN_PLAN.model = "all"`; only create/edit gated; unknown plan fails closed |
| Foundation (r13) | `assets3d/manifest.ts`, `asset-profile.ts`, `asset-jobs.ts` | glTF + sidecar, legal ledger, `libraryEligible`, `WORKER_CLASSES`, in-memory queue + object store (no DB tables yet) |

## 2. Architecture per layer
| Layer | Serves | Canonical data | Human edits | Runtime |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| L1 viewport + paint | every model | `ModelDoc` + `TextureDoc` per texture (reused) | paint, fill face, pick, decals | three.js (MIT) client, lazy route chunk |
| L2 cuboid + bone editor | MC creatures (RigSpec), MC 3D items (`ItemCuboidSpec`), Hytale | RigSpec v1.1 / ItemCuboidSpec v1 | cubes, bones, pivots, UV boxes, keys | client ops on the spec; compile server-side |
| L3 retexture + light edit | FiveM/RedM liveries, later GMod/Zomboid, Palworld/ARK | glTF 2.0 + sidecar, per-channel lossless layers | layers, decal transforms, material values, small transforms | client; unwrap/convert/pack on workers |
| L4 AI mesh | hard-surface and organic props | glTF + sidecar (`ai-mesh`) | transform, material, UV tweaks only (no sculpting) | `linux-cpu` Blender or `gpu` worker |

### Data model additions (Cyrus-prefixed, opaque ids, no FKs into Nxeon)
| Addition | Shape | Why |
|---|---|---|

| RigSpec **v1.1** (additive) | optional cube `id`, `uv: [u,v]` pin, `skin.paint` ref | stable ids for merge; pinned UV keeps paint in place. Needs compiler rig-c2 + regenerated build-service copy (strict schema rejects new keys) |
| `ItemCuboidSpec` v1 (new) | elements from/to, single-axis rotation, per-face UV auto/pinned, materials, decal layers; links `ItemModelSpec` states | the real 3D gun; emits one model JSON per state into the existing pack |
| `CyrusModelDraft` | `projectId, ownerRef, assetKey, baseAssetId, baseHeadId, doc, updatedAt`, unique per owner+key | autosave, not a revision |
| `CyrusAssetJob`, `CyrusObject` | DB backing for r13 `JobQueue` / `ObjectStore` | workers, previews, exports |
| `CyrusPreviewRender` | key = sha(specSha + renderer + preset) → object key | cache |
| `CyrusLibraryAsset`, `CyrusLibraryReport` | `assetSha, kind, creatorRef, state, filters Json, legalClass, licenceVersion` | community asset library (today's `CyrusLibraryItem` is a mod-page bookmark, a different thing) |
| `AssetProfile.meshBudget` (proposed) | `{maxTriangles, lods: number[], maxMaterials}` | L4 cleanup target and checks |
| manifest `provenance.generator` (proposed) | `"ai-mesh" \| "ai-spec" \| "studio" \| …` | flags AI-mesh output; library + filters read it |

### Save, revisions, undo, autosave, AI edits
| Concern | Design |
|---|---|
| Undo/redo | client op log on the `ModelDoc`; reuse `History<T>` (200 steps); one gizmo drag / stroke / accepted candidate = one step |
| Autosave | debounce 5 s idle, max 30 s, to `CyrusModelDraft`; reload restores; drafts are never built or shared |
| Save | explicit "Save revision": validate (spec + quality) → compile → revision kind `asset` + asset row; `expectedHeadId` → 409 stale_head, same as textures |
| AI edit mid-session | AI never touches the working copy. It returns a candidate built from base revision R. If the user has unsaved edits: 3-way merge per node id (bone, cube, key, layer); disjoint changes merge, overlaps listed ("1 overlap"); human wins by default; Apply / Apply part / Reject (mockup b) |
| AI writes, human fixes | prompt → spec (never raw mesh, never UVs) → deterministic render + look check → user opens it and fixes; each save is a revision (mockup f) |

## 7. L4: AI mesh generation (owner addition)
| Route | How | Quality / cost (all U) |
|---|---|---|
| (a) Script geometry | Claude writes Blender-Python (bmesh, modifiers, bevels, booleans) run headless in a sandboxed `linux-cpu` worker (no network, allow-listed modules, 10 min cap); render 6 views → vision model compares to the prompt → Claude revises the script, max 4 passes | best for hard-surface (guns, crates, lanterns); token cost per pass unknown; organic shapes weak |
| (b) Parts library | Cyrus-owned kits (receiver, barrel, stock, grip, magazine; wheels, cabins) assembled by script with sockets | the main quality lever; needs authoring time; parts are `platform-library` class |
| (c) Image/text-to-3D | self-hosted TRELLIS (MIT) on a `gpu` worker; Meshy/Tripo only with owner spend approval; Hunyuan3D excluded (licence excludes EU/UK/KR) | blobby topology, no rig, unknown UVs; always goes through cleanup |
| Cleanup (all routes) | decimate/retopo to `meshBudget.maxTriangles`; xatlas UV; bake normal (and AO) from the high-poly; LOD chain per `meshBudget.lods`; manifold, watertight, UV-overlap, scale/units checks | fails closed: an asset that misses budget or checks is not saved |
Lands in: `AssetProfile.meshBudget`, manifest `provenance.generator: "ai-mesh"`, legal class `ai-generated-for-user`. Human step stays: transform, material values, UV tweaks in Model Studio, never sculpting (mockup a, `?mesh=1`). Not for Minecraft Java (no meshes); useful for FiveM props and later UE games.

## 8. What Claude can and cannot produce (say this in the product)
| Layer | Realistic | Not |
|---|---|---|
| L2 | blocky items, creatures, props for MC and Hytale | smooth/organic shapes |
| L1 | paint, stickers, decals, wear | photo-real textures |
| L3 | realistic vehicles/clothing **only** as a retexture of a template the user supplies | new realistic meshes, anything shipping the base mesh |
| L4 | stylised or simple hard-surface props within a budget | rigged characters, hero assets, guaranteed likeness |
Quality for every row is unverified until the paid eval (100 owner-labelled samples, the existing vision-judge plan).

## 9. Community asset library (owner decisions: automatic, not opt-in)
- **Flow:** asset saved → if `libraryEligible(manifest)` → `pending checks` → filters → `published` or `held for review` → (report) → `removed`. States shown as badges in the studio and "My contributions" (mockup e).
- **Never enters:** game-derived, third-party-licensed, imported. **Gap found (V):** `libraryEligible` only excludes `provenance.source === "import"`; a file the user **uploaded** is `source: "user"` and passes. Add an `uploaded` source (or flag). Also exclude anything whose `derivedFrom` hits a game-derived hash (a livery is only meaningful on the game's mesh).
- **Filters (lib-1):** provenance, trademark/logo (text + vision), real-weapon names (AK-47, Glock... a hold, not a block), adult content (vision on 6 renders), near-copy of known game assets (perceptual hash vs a reference set). All thresholds U.
- **Rights:** licence grant in the Terms of Service at sign-up and repeated in the studio; creator keeps copyright; attribution `@handle` kept in pack credits; report + takedown queue with a person; removal does not break mods already using the asset (U: owner decision).
- **Gate:** browsing open to all; "Use in project" = asset create → follows `canAsset` for the kind (today: model/texture = All models, sound = Saka). The owner's "usable by anyone" conflicts with this; decision needed.

## 10. Plan placement (proposal, owner decides)
Model Studio paint, edit and retexture at **All models** (matches `ASSET_MIN_PLAN.model`). Never gated: view, orbit, in-game preview, install, export, rebuild, Mod Packs, import, library browsing. Server checks every create/edit; unknown plan fails closed for edits only. Alternative: give Saka **paint-only** on existing models (cheap upsell) — it writes textures, so it would contradict the Texture Studio gate.

## 3. Architecture needed now

**Canonical asset model (decision):** glTF 2.0 (meshes, UV sets, skeleton, metallic-roughness PBR) plus a Cyrus sidecar manifest (provenance, legal class, per-slot role, units). Alternatives rejected: USD (heavy, no web viewer ecosystem), FBX (proprietary SDK), engine-native formats (lock-in). **Store channels as separate lossless layers** (albedo sRGB, normal, roughness, metallic, AO, emissive, height, masks) and **pack only at export** per engine. Units: metres, +Y up (glTF); the adapter converts axis/handedness.

**Per-engine packing (adapter's job; all U, verify per game before shipping):**

| Target | Typical channel convention |
|---|---|
| Unreal (Palworld, ARK) | BaseColor, Normal (DirectX, -Y), ORM pack (AO/Rough/Metal) |
| Unity (Unturned) | Metallic in R, smoothness in alpha; OpenGL normal |
| Source (GMod) | VTF DXT1/DXT5, `$basetexture`/`$bumpmap`, phong masks |
| GTA/RAGE (FiveM) | Diffuse + normal + spec in YTD (DDS inside RSC container) |
| Fallout 4 | DDS BC7 diffuse, BC5 normal (V: nexusmods Fallout 4 guides via search) |
| Hytale | PNG per model (flat albedo, U) |

**Libraries (licence verified from repo LICENSE/GitHub API on 2026-10-10 unless marked):**

| Need | Pick | Licence | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| BCn encode (Windows worker) | DirectXTex `texconv`, DirectXMesh | MIT (V) | Windows exe, ok in worker |
| BCn/KTX2 on Linux | Basis Universal (UASTC/ETC1S, BC7 transcode) | Apache-2.0 (V) | also web delivery |
| KTX2 tooling | KTX-Software | Apache-2.0 for repo files, third-party mixed (V) | check bundled deps |
| Compressonator | GPUOpen | no licence detected by GitHub (U: MIT in practice) | avoid until checked |
| Mesh optimise/LOD | meshoptimizer | MIT (V) | |
| UV unwrap/atlas | xatlas | MIT (V) | |
| Import/convert | assimp | BSD-style (V header) | |
| glTF processing | glTF-Transform / gltf-pipeline | Apache-2.0 (gltf-pipeline V; glTF-Transform U) | |
| Viewer | three.js | MIT (V) | server-side preview via headless Chromium or a small Node renderer |
| Heavy DCC | Blender headless, **separate process only** | GPL (V "NOASSERTION", GPL in practice U) | glTF-Blender-IO Apache-2.0 (V) |
| Do not embed/ship | Blockbench (GPL-3, V), Sollumz (GPL-3, V), CodeWalker (no licence, V), Crowbar (none found) | | Run only in isolated workers on user data, never redistribute; legal review before CodeWalker use |

**Windows build worker:** one more worker class beside node-2 Linux builds. Ephemeral VM per job (or snapshot revert), no outbound network except the broker, **pull-based** job queue, signed job manifest, allow-listed tools only, hard timeout and CPU/RAM caps, no Proxmox or Nxeon credentials on the guest, outputs returned through object storage and re-scanned on Linux (format validators, size caps, forbidden-content scan). Game installs (Creation Kit, UE dev kits, GTA files) are legal-gated: only if the game's EULA allows hosted use (U for all); default = user supplies templates.

**AI texturing (reality check):**

| Option | Facts | Use |
|---|---|---|
| LLM spec + procedural/deterministic render (existing approach) | cheap, reproducible | default; masks per UV region from adapter |
| Image model into UV space with region masks, then seamless tiling | image models do not understand UVs; works with masks/templates | texture lane |
| PBR estimation | Material Palette (MIT, V search); normals from height and heuristic roughness are deterministic and free | derive channels, do not hallucinate them |
| Meshy / Tripo APIs | paid plans own the output; Meshy free tier is CC BY 4.0 (V: docs.meshy.ai/en/webapp/pricing; tripo3d.ai blog); low-poly modes exist, quality claims are vendor marketing | prototype props only, per-call cost |
| Hunyuan3D-2 | Community licence **excludes EU, UK, South Korea** and forbids using outputs to train other models (V: repo LICENSE) | **NO** |
| TRELLIS | MIT (V api) | optional self-host prop prototypes; still no game-ready topology/UV/rig |

Text-to-3D gives static prop blobs, not game-ready characters or vehicles: no rig, wrong topology, unknown UVs. Do not promise it.

**Storage/jobs:** S3-compatible content-addressed store (sha256 keys), 4K PBR sets run 100+ MB uncompressed so cap per tenant and store derivatives lazily. Jobs get a `workerClass` (`linux-cpu`, `windows-tools`, `gpu`); start API-based for image models, no own GPU cluster.

**Asset-profile contract fields each adapter declares:**
`game, engineFamily, meshFormats[], textureFormats[], compression[] (BC1/3/5/7, PNG), channelMap{role->file/channel}, normalConvention, colorSpace per slot, maxRes/budget per class, uvRules (reuse-template vs new), skeletonPolicy (reuse|none|forbidden), packaging (zip, pak, ytd, gma, asset pack), delivery (server-streamed | workshop-user-publishes | workshop-platform-publishes | client-manual | none), workerClass, requiredGameFiles (none|user-supplied|platform-licensed), legal{ policyUrl, commercialOk, aiOk, redistributeBase:false, monetisationRule, attestationRequired, retrievedAt }, validators[], previewShader, maturity`.

**Legal ledger rule:** every asset row carries a class: `user-original`, `ai-generated-for-user`, `platform-library` (Nxeon-owned/CC0 only), `third-party-licensed`, or `game-derived`. **Game-derived assets are never stored beyond the job, never added to any library, never redistributed**; deliverables must contain only user-original or delta content (a retexture ships the texture, not the base mesh). A per-game policy flag (from the table above, with source URL and date) gates export, commercial sharing and the community library; owner reviews each policy page when it changes.

Since the catalog agent already adds its own budget field to AssetProfile, I want to avoid stepping on the same lines and causing a merge conflict, so I'm considering keeping my mesh budget logic isolated in its own module and exposing it through a helper function instead of editing the shared type directly.

Since there's no mesh-capable game profile yet, I'll need a fixture profile for testing the triangle-budget flow — something like a generic glTF prop profile with an explicitly labelled draft budget, kept separate from real game adapters so it's clear the numbers are unverified. I'm now working out the module structure under the meshgen directory to house this.

I'm sketching out `spec.ts` with Zod schemas covering common fields, per-template specs, kit assembly, and scratch-route requests, plus the overall MeshgenRequest shape. Then `templates.ts` holds the template and kit registries with their spec schemas and metadata, and `router.ts` defines the deterministic routing logic that decides which rung to use based on prompt, category, game, and available resources.

Now I'm outlining `cost.ts` for token/dollar estimation per rung, `catalog.ts` for the catalog matching interface, `scan.ts` for scanning scratch scripts against allow/deny rules, and `runner.ts` defining the BlenderRunner interface along with a remote execution implementation.

For the runner itself, I'm reusing the SSH client tarball helper and setting up per-job directories on the remote host with isolated in/work/home subfolders, using a flock-guarded sandbox script to run the job and then collecting the resulting work directory as a base64-encoded tarball over stdout to avoid binary corruption.

For postprocess.ts, I'm designing checks that combine the Blender harness's stats JSON (triangle counts, nonmanifold geometry, shells, UVs, materials, bbox) with an independent GLB parser in TypeScript that validates the header and accessor counts against those stats, then enforces budget limits per category — with the harness decimating over-budget meshes when the spec allows it and failing closed with structured issues if still over budget after that.

Now I'm thinking through the manifest output — building an AssetManifest with geometry hash and provenance fields, plus a separate MeshgenRecord object (since the manifest schema is strict) to hold rung, template, token usage, render keys, stats, and timings, with output keys spanning the glb, manifest, record, and renders.

For worker.ts, I'm realizing the in-memory queue's claim function doesn't filter by job type, only by class, so a meshgen-only worker could end up claiming unrelated jobs — I need to add type filtering to the claim logic.

The fix I'm settling on is adding an optional `types` filter to the claim parameters, keeping it backwards-compatible, then building out `runMeshgenWorker` and `processOneMeshgenJob` with timeout handling via a race against the deadline plus periodic sweeps, discarding outputs if the job expired mid-run, and gating the whole worker behind a CYRUS_MESHGEN environment flag.

I'm also planning a separate CYRUS_MESHGEN_SCRATCH flag for the rung 3 feature, defining the model-facing tool contracts (meshgen_estimate, meshgen_submit) with their schemas, and laying out the Python Blender harness files that dispatch requests to template modules for generating geometry, parts kits, and specific templates like rifle, crate, and sword.

I'm clarifying rung distinctions: rung 1 is a parametric template with fixed structure and numeric/enum parameters, while rung 2 is kit assembly where the model emits a list of parts with placement and transform data for cases the templates can't handle.

Rung 2's JSON is bigger but more flexible, so I'll design it as a general assembly spec: a list of parts, each either a geometric primitive (box/cylinder/prism/rod with dimensions and slot info) or a named kit variant, placed via offsets — general enough for any hard-surface object.

Since the task wants parts-kit assembly where JSON picks variants, I'll structure the kit as named parts with selectable variants, like receiver, grip, magazine, stock, and handguard options pulled from a rifle kit template.

I'll settle on a generic hard-surface kit with roughly 14 part variants plus mirroring, since JSON-only deterministic kit assembly handles misfits like lanterns, barrels, and tables well.

For rung 3's scratch scripting, the harness executes the model's code in a namespace exposing Part, make_materials, bpy, bmesh, math, and Vector, requiring a build() function that returns objects, with static scanning to block disallowed imports.

I need to deny dangerous names and attributes (os, sys, subprocess, exec, eval, dunder access, risky bpy.ops calls, file/io/threading modules) and enforce script size and line caps, with the scan happening both in TS before shipping and potentially duplicated via Python's ast module for stronger validation.

I'll combine both: a cheap TS token scan at submission time and a stronger Python AST walk inside the sandbox right before exec, checking imports against an allowlist, blocking underscore-prefixed attribute access, denylisted names, and calls to dangerous builtins. I'll also strip dangerous builtins from the exec namespace, treating this as defense-in-depth rather than the actual security boundary — that's the sandbox's job. On timing, real Cycles renders take about 26 seconds at 32 samples per pixel, which matters for the meshgen service's preview-based vision step.

For post-processing, I'm planning bmesh checks per object — triangle counts, non-manifold edges, shell count, UV presence and bounds, zero-area faces, loose vertices, material count, bounding box — then auto-decimating anything over budget by applying a collapse modifier scaled to hit the target ratio before recounting. The TS layer then re-validates against the AssetProfile budgets and independently parses the GLB itself, checking the header, JSON/BIN chunks, accessor bounds, and triangle counts against the stats reported by Blender, possibly layering in the Khronos gltf-validator for extra confidence.

Separately I'm sketching manifest validation rules (assetId pattern, safe geometry path) and the token/rung accounting structure that records estimate versus actual usage per generation attempt.

I want this token model documented with clear sourcing so it's traceable to real measurements rather than guesses.

Then I need to design pricing config with per-million-token input/output/cache rates, falling back to a "price not configured" note when null, and decide whether Cyrus's own token economy needs separate handling or if I should just scope this to model token/dollar estimation. I'm also setting hard caps per rung, like rung 3 capping at 4 rounds, 24KB scripts, and 30k tokens.

For routing, I'm laying out a deterministic decision tree: first check if the catalog matcher has a high-confidence match for rung 0, otherwise fall back to keyword/category matching against enabled templates, scoring by keyword hits with exact category matches winning.

I need to look at the existing crate and parts scripts before writing tpl_crate.py and tpl_sword.py.

For the worker setup, I'm defining a linux-cpu job type "meshgen" that takes a request key input and produces glb, manifest, record, and render outputs. For end-to-end testing on node-2, I'm planning a flight script that enqueues jobs on an in-memory queue, runs the worker via the node2 runner, and logs results to a flights JSON file, invoked lightly over SSH from the primary.

I'm now weighing how that flight script should actually execute on node-2 — whether it needs to SSH to itself, use a local exec abstraction, or go through devhost, and checking what user context devhost runs under since systemd-run needs root. I'm leaning toward treating this as a lightweight process rather than a heavy build, though the rules may require heavy commands to go through devhost.

#!/bin/bash
# =============================================================================
# devhost — run agent dev work on the BUILD HOST (node-2), not on the primary.
#
# Edit files on the primary as usual (your own git worktree — never /opt/nxeon),
# then run every heavy command through this helper. It mirrors your worktree's
# source to node-2 (/tank/nxeon-build/wt/<name>, own node_modules there), runs the
# command inside the capped nxeon-build-agents.slice with a THROWAWAY database
# (Postgres on node-2 127.0.0.1:5433), and streams the output back.
#
#   scripts/devhost run [--lock] [--max SEC] -- CMD...   push + run CMD in the node-2 copy
#   scripts/devhost tsc                                  = run -- npx tsc --noEmit
#   scripts/devhost test [FILES...]                      = run --lock -- npx tsx --test ...
#   scripts/devhost build                                = run --lock -- npx next build
#   scripts/devhost dev [--port P]                       start `next dev` on node-2 (background unit)
#   scripts/devhost bg NAME [--port P] -- CMD...         any background process (worker, preview server)
#   scripts/devhost stop [NAME|all]                      stop this worktree's background units
#   scripts/devhost logs [NAME] [-n N] [-f]              journal of a background unit (default: dev)
#   scripts/devhost tunnel PORT [LOCAL_PORT]             ssh -L so the primary can curl/Playwright it
#   scripts/devhost pull REMOTE_PATH [LOCAL_DEST]        copy results (screenshots, reports) back
#   scripts/devhost push                                 just sync files (run does this itself)
#   scripts/devhost install                              force npm install + prisma generate there
#   scripts/devhost db push|reset|info                   throwaway DB: schema push / recreate / name
#   scripts/devhost env set KEY=VALUE | unset KEY | list extra env for this worktree (never prod secrets)
#   scripts/devhost rm                                   stop units, drop the throwaway DB, delete the node-2 copy
#   scripts/devhost ls | status | sync                   workspaces / node-2 load / push refs to node-2's mirror
#
# Rules: /root/agent-notes/BUILD-HOST.md. The node-2 copy is a build/run sandbox,
# not a place to edit or commit — your primary-side worktree stays the source of truth.
# =============================================================================
set -euo pipefail
HERE="$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")"
# shellcheck source=lib/buildhost-env.sh
source "$HERE/lib/buildhost-env.sh"
REPO="${DEVHOST_REPO:-/opt/nxeon}"

die() { echo "devhost: $*" >&2; exit 1; }
say() { echo "devhost: $*" >&2; }
q() { printf '%q ' "$@"; }

# ---- workspace identity -----------------------------------------------------
worktree_root() {
  local top; top=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null) || die "run this inside your own git worktree of the Nxeon repo"
  top=$(readlink -f "$top")
  case "$top" in
    /opt/nxeon|/opt/nxeon-staging|/tank/nxeon-deploy/*) die "$top is a live/deploy tree. Create your own worktree first:  git -C /opt/nxeon worktree add /tank/dev-worktrees/<name> -b <branch> main" ;;
  esac
  [ -L "$top/.next" ] && die "$top/.next is a symlink (a live tree) — refusing"
  [ -L "$top/node_modules" ] && say "warning: $top/node_modules is a symlink — never 'git add -A' here (see BUILD-HOST.md). devhost does not need local node_modules at all."
  echo "$top"
}
ws_name() {
  local top="$1" n
  n=$(basename "$top" | tr 'A-Z' 'a-z' | tr -c 'a-z0-9-\n' '-' | sed -E 's/-+/-/g; s/^-//; s/-$//' | cut -c1-40)
  [ -n "$n" ] || n=wt
  echo "${DEVHOST_NAME:-$n}"
}
init_ws() {
  TOP=$(worktree_root); NAME=$(ws_name "$TOP")
  case "$NAME" in *[!a-z0-9-]*|"") die "bad workspace name '$NAME' (DEVHOST_NAME=...)";; esac

#!/bin/bash
# Run a command on node-2 INSIDE the capped build slice. Runs ON node-2.
# Called by scripts/devhost and scripts/lib/buildhost.sh from the primary.
#
#   run-capped.sh agents|prod [options] -- CMD [ARGS...]
#     --dir DIR        working directory (default /)
#     --unit NAME      transient unit name (default nxeon-run-<pid>)
#     --bg             start as a background service (dev servers); prints the unit
#                      name and returns. Stop with: systemctl stop NAME
#     --max SEC        RuntimeMaxSec (default 7200 foreground, 14400 --bg)
#     --env FILE       extra KEY=VALUE environment file (root-only), e.g. a worktree's
#                      dev env. NEVER a production .env.
#     --lock           hold /run/lock/nxeon-build.lock (one heavy job on node-2 at a
#                      time — `next build`, full test suites, Playwright suites)
#
# Foreground commands run as a transient SERVICE with --pipe --wait so CPU/memory
# accounting is reported when they finish, and they never leave the slice.
# Every process gets nice 10, ionice best-effort 7 and oom_score_adj 1000 (agents)
# / 500 (release builds), so if node-2 ever runs out of memory the kernel kills
# build/dev processes, never a customer VM (qemu processes keep their default 0).
set -euo pipefail
SLICE_KIND="${1:-}"; shift || true
case "$SLICE_KIND" in

props=(--slice="$SLICE" -p Nice=10 -p IOSchedulingClass=best-effort -p IOSchedulingPriority=7

       -E npm_config_update_notifier=false -E TMPDIR=/tank/nxeon-build/tmp)
[ -n "$ENVF" ] && props+=(-p EnvironmentFile="$ENVF")

if [ "$LOCK" = 1 ]; then
  exec 7>>/run/lock/nxeon-build.lock

    flock -w "${BUILD_LOCK_WAIT_SEC:-1800}" 7 || { echo "timed out waiting for the build lock" >&2; exit 75; }

  echo "$UNIT"
  exit 0
fi

# pk_parts.py -- PARTS KIT: reusable variants. Each fn(P, S, A): P=dict of Parts, S=its spec section, A=shared anchor dict.
# Frame: +X muzzle, Z up, bore axis z=0, y=0 centreline, metres. Receiver rear face at x=0.
import math
from mathutils import Vector

def g(S, k, d): return S.get(k, d) if S else d
def shear(pts, k): return [(x + z * k, z) for x, z in pts]

# ---------------- RECEIVERS (set anchors) ----------------
def recv_ak(P, S, A):
    R = P['receiver']; L = g(S, 'length', 0.36); h = g(S, 'height', 0.07); w = g(S, 'width', 0.046); zc = -0.017
    R.box((L / 2, 0, zc), (L, w, h), 'body', 0.004)
    R.cyl((L / 2, 0, 0.014), w / 2 + 0.0005, L - 0.01, 'body', seg=20)
    R.box((L + 0.012, 0, 0.0), (0.04, w - 0.004, 0.06), 'body', 0.005)
    R.box((L * 0.5, w / 2 + 0.002, -0.012), (L * 0.5, 0.004, 0.022), 'dark', 0.002)
    R.cyl((L * 0.62, w / 2 + 0.007, 0.018), 0.006, 0.04, 'dark', axis='y', seg=10)
    R.cyl((L * 0.62, w / 2 + 0.029, 0.018), 0.011, 0.014, 'dark', axis='y', seg=12)
    A.update(x0=0, x1=L + 0.032, z_top=0.0385, zb=zc - h / 2, w=w, zmid=zc, grip_x=0.062, trig_x=0.168, mag_x=L - 0.09,
             mag_z=zc - h / 2 + 0.005, sight_x=L - 0.08, hg_x0=L - 0.005)

def _rail(R, x0, L, z, slot='barrel', wd=0.02):
    R.box((x0 + L / 2, 0, z), (L, wd, 0.008), slot)
    for i in range(int(L / 0.022)):
        R.box((x0 + 0.011 + i * 0.022, 0, z + 0.006), (0.011, wd, 0.005), slot)

def recv_modern(P, S, A):
    R = P['receiver']; L = g(S, 'length', 0.30); w = 0.042
    R.box((L / 2, 0, 0.022), (L, w - 0.004, 0.048), 'body', 0.003)
    R.box((L * 0.45, 0, -0.032), (L * 0.9, w, 0.062), 'body', 0.003)
    R.box((L * 0.68, 0, -0.082), (L * 0.30, w - 0.004, 0.04), 'body', 0.003)
    R.box((L * 0.5, w / 2 - 0.002 + 0.0006, 0.02), (L * 0.26, 0.002, 0.02), 'dark')
    R.box((-0.012, 0, 0.04), (0.03, 0.026, 0.012), 'dark', 0.002)
    R.cyl((L + 0.005, 0, 0), 0.022, 0.02, 'body', seg=16)
    _rail(R, 0.0, L, 0.050)
    A.update(x0=0, x1=L + 0.015, z_top=0.0595, zb=-0.063, w=w, zmid=0.0, grip_x=0.055, trig_x=0.145, mag_x=L * 0.68,
             mag_z=-0.062, sight_x=L * 0.5, hg_x0=L - 0.01)

def recv_smg(P, S, A):
    R = P['receiver']; L = g(S, 'length', 0.27); w = g(S, 'width', 0.05); h = 0.062
    R.box((L / 2, 0, -0.002), (L, w, h), 'body', 0.007)
    R.box((L / 2, 0, h / 2 - 0.002 + 0.0008), (L * 0.9, 0.018, 0.004), 'dark')
    R.box((-0.006, 0, -0.002), (0.02, w - 0.006, h - 0.008), 'body', 0.004)
    R.cyl((L + 0.008, 0, 0), 0.028, 0.02, 'body', seg=16)
    R.box((L * 0.4, w / 2 + 0.0006, 0.004), (L * 0.22, 0.002, 0.018), 'dark')
    R.cyl((L * 0.55, w / 2 + 0.008, 0.012), 0.005, 0.016, 'dark', axis='y', seg=8)
    R.cyl((L * 0.55, w / 2 + 0.02, 0.012), 0.009, 0.01, 'dark', axis='y', seg=10)
    gx = L * 0.55
    A.update(x0=0, x1=L + 0.018, z_top=h / 2 - 0.002, zb=-0.002 - h / 2, w=w, zmid=-0.002, grip_x=gx, trig_x=gx + 0.075,
             mag_x=gx, mag_z=-0.002 - h / 2, sight_x=L * 0.15, hg_x0=L - 0.01, mag_in_grip=True)

def recv_bullpup(P, S, A):
    R = P['receiver']; L = g(S, 'length', 0.52); w = g(S, 'width', 0.05)
    pts = [(0, 0.04), (0.04, 0.06), (L * 0.55, 0.06), (L, 0.054), (L, -0.05), (L * 0.6, -0.06), (L * 0.33, -0.072), (0.03, -0.085), (0, -0.075)]
    R.prism(pts, w, 'body', 0.005)
    R.box((L * 0.34, w / 2 + 0.0006, 0.0), (L * 0.14, 0.002, 0.04), 'dark')
    if g(S, 'rail', True): _rail(R, L * 0.2, L * 0.7, 0.062)
    gx = L * 0.52
    A.update(x0=0, x1=L, z_top=0.0725 if g(S, 'rail', True) else 0.06, zb=-0.07, w=w, zmid=-0.01, grip_x=gx, trig_x=gx + 0.075,
             mag_x=gx - 0.115, mag_z=-0.07, sight_x=L * 0.42, hg_x0=L - 0.02, bullpup=True)
RECV = {'ak_stamped': recv_ak, 'modern_slab': recv_modern, 'smg_boxy': recv_smg, 'bullpup_shell': recv_bullpup}

# ---------------- GRIPS ----------------
def grip_ak(P, S, A):
    ln = g(S, 'length', 0.14); rk = g(S, 'rake', 0.38); zb = A['zb']
    P['grip'].box((A['grip_x'], 0, zb - ln / 2 + 0.018), (0.048, 0.046, ln), 'furniture', 0.009, rot=(0, rk, 0))
    A['grip_rake'] = rk
def grip_poly(P, S, A):
    ln = g(S, 'length', 0.13); rk = g(S, 'rake', 0.30); s = ln / 0.13; wd = g(S, 'width', 0.042)
    pts = [(-0.022, 0.01), (0.026, 0.01), (0.027, -0.03 * s), (0.022, -0.055 * s), (0.03, -0.085 * s), (0.022, -ln), (-0.03, -ln), (-0.026, -0.09 * s), (-0.032, -0.05 * s), (-0.024, -0.02 * s)]
    pts = [(x + A['grip_x'], z + A['zb'] + 0.01) for x, z in shear(pts, math.tan(rk))]
    P['grip'].prism(pts, wd, 'furniture', 0.004); A['grip_rake'] = rk
def grip_vertical(P, S, A):
    ln = g(S, 'length', 0.11)
    P['grip'].box((A['grip_x'], 0, A['zb'] - ln / 2 + 0.01), (0.044, 0.04, ln), 'furniture', 0.006)
    P['grip'].box((A['grip_x'], 0, A['zb'] - ln + 0.012), (0.05, 0.046, 0.012), 'dark', 0.003); A['grip_rake'] = 0.0
def grip_none(P, S, A): A['grip_rake'] = 0.0
GRIP = {'ak_slanted': grip_ak, 'raked_poly': grip_poly, 'vertical': grip_vertical, 'none': grip_none}

def trigger_guard(P, S, A):
    G = P['grip']; tx = A['trig_x']; zb = A['zb']; s = g(S, 'guard_scale', 1.0)
    dx = [-0.058, -0.056, -0.038, 0.027, 0.046, 0.048, 0.04, 0.038, 0.024, -0.036, -0.048, -0.05]
    dz = [0.006, -0.042, -0.053, -0.053, -0.035, 0.006, 0.006, -0.033, -0.045, -0.045, -0.037, 0.006]
    G.prism([(tx + x * s, zb + z * s) for x, z in zip(dx, dz)], 0.012, 'barrel', 0.0015)
    G.box((tx, 0, zb - 0.022), (0.006, 0.006, 0.034), 'barrel', 0.0015, rot=(0, -0.3, 0))

# ---------------- MAGAZINES ----------------
def mag_curved(P, S, A):
    cap = g(S, 'capacity', 30); arc = g(S, 'arc_length', 0.10 + cap * 0.0036); deg = g(S, 'curve_deg', 46); w = g(S, 'width', 0.04)
    R = arc / math.radians(deg); x0, z0 = A['mag_x'], A['mag_z']; N = 10; back, front = [], []
    for i in range(N + 1):
        ph = math.radians(deg) * i / N; cx, cz = x0 + R * (1 - math.cos(ph)), z0 - R * math.sin(ph)
        nx, nz = math.cos(ph), math.sin(ph); h = 0.026 + 0.008 * i / N
        back.append((cx - nx * h, cz - nz * h)); front.append((cx + nx * h, cz + nz * h))
    P['magazine'].prism(back + front[::-1], w, 'mag', 0.004)
    ph = math.radians(deg) * 0.5; A['mag_mid'] = (x0 + R * (1 - math.cos(ph)), z0 - R * math.sin(ph), -ph, w)
def mag_box(P, S, A):
    cap = g(S, 'capacity', 30); ln = g(S, 'length', 0.06 + cap * 0.0055); hd = g(S, 'depth', 0.024); w = g(S, 'width', 0.038)
    c = math.radians(g(S, 'cant_deg', 8))
    if A.get('mag_in_grip'): c = -A.get('grip_rake', 0.0); hd = min(hd, 0.02); w = min(w, 0.036)
    T = Vector((A['mag_x'], A['mag_z'])); d = Vector((math.sin(c), -math.cos(c))); n = Vector((math.cos(c), math.sin(c))); B = T + d * ln
    pts = [tuple(T - n * hd), tuple(T + n * hd), tuple(B + n * hd), tuple(B - n * hd)]
    P['magazine'].prism(pts, w, 'mag', 0.003)
    P['magazine'].box((B.x, 0, B.y + 0.004), (hd * 2 + 0.006, w + 0.004, 0.014), 'mag', 0.002, rot=(0, -c, 0))
    M = (T + B) / 2; A['mag_mid'] = (M.x, M.y, -c, w); A['mag_len'] = ln
def mag_drum(P, S, A):
    cap = g(S, 'capacity', 50); R = g(S, 'radius', 0.05 + cap * 0.0006); w = g(S, 'width', 0.055); cx, cz = A['mag_x'] + 0.012, A['mag_z'] - R - 0.022
    M = P['magazine']
    M.box((A['mag_x'], 0, A['mag_z'] - 0.012), (0.04, 0.04, 0.03), 'mag', 0.003)
    M.cyl((cx, 0, cz), R, w, 'mag', axis='y', seg=24, bevel=0.004)
    for sgn in (-1, 1): M.cyl((cx, sgn * (w / 2 - 0.002), cz), R * 0.8, 0.006, 'accent', axis='y', seg=20)
    M.cyl((cx, 0, cz), 0.018, w + 0.012, 'accent', axis='y', seg=12)
    A['mag_mid'] = (cx, cz, 0.0, w); A['mag_drum'] = True
MAG = {'curved': mag_curved, 'straight_box': mag_box, 'drum': mag_drum}

# ---------------- STOCKS ----------------
def stock_wood(P, S, A):
    Ls = g(S, 'length', 0.22); w = g(S, 'width', 0.04); St = P['stock']
    St.prism([(0.01, 0.03), (0.01 - Ls, 0.012), (0.005 - Ls, -0.112), (0.01 - 0.59 * Ls, -0.09), (0.01, -0.064)], w, 'furniture', 0.006)
    St.box((0.008 - Ls, 0, -0.05), (0.012, 0.042, 0.134), 'barrel', 0.003, rot=(0, -0.05, 0)); A['stock_len'] = Ls
def stock_poly(P, S, A):
    L = g(S, 'length', 0.24); w = g(S, 'width', 0.044); St = P['stock']
    St.cyl((-L * 0.25, 0, -0.004), 0.019, L * 0.6, 'body', seg=12)
    St.prism([(-L * 0.4, 0.04), (-L * 0.4, 0.05), (-L, 0.058), (-L, -0.09), (-L + 0.02, -0.095), (-L * 0.62, -0.04), (-L * 0.4, -0.03)], w, 'furniture', 0.004)
    St.box((-L - 0.004, 0, -0.016), (0.012, w + 0.004, 0.158), 'dark', 0.004); A['stock_len'] = L
def stock_wire(P, S, A):
    L = g(S, 'length', 0.24); St = P['stock']; wy = A['w'] / 2 + 0.008; zm = A['zmid'] + 0.012; folded = g(S, 'folded', False)
    sg = 1 if folded else -1; r = 0.0042; zb = zm - 0.075; xe = sg * L
    for s in (-1, 1):
        St.rod((0, s * wy, zm), (xe, s * wy, zm), r, 'barrel'); St.rod((xe * 0.35, s * wy, zm), (xe, s * wy, zb + 0.01), r, 'barrel')
        St.cyl((0.0, s * wy, zm), 0.009, 0.014, 'barrel', seg=10)
    St.rod((xe, -wy, zb + 0.01), (xe, wy, zb + 0.01), r, 'barrel')
    St.box((xe + sg * 0.004, 0, zm - 0.036), (0.012, wy * 2 + 0.01, 0.094), 'dark', 0.003); A['stock_len'] = L
def stock_strut(P, S, A):
    L = g(S, 'length', 0.22); St = P['stock']; wy = A['w'] / 2 + 0.01; zm = A['zmid']; folded = g(S, 'folded', False)
    sg = 1 if folded else -1; xe = sg * L
    for s in (-1, 1):
        St.box((xe / 2, s * wy, zm + 0.008), (L, 0.01, 0.02), 'body', 0.003)
        St.cyl((0, s * wy, zm + 0.008), 0.014, 0.016, 'barrel', axis='y', seg=14)
    St.prism([(xe, zm + 0.04), (xe + sg * 0.012, zm + 0.04), (xe + sg * 0.02, zm - 0.07), (xe, zm - 0.075)], 2 * wy, 'dark', 0.003)
    A['stock_len'] = L
def stock_bullpup(P, S, A):
    St = P['stock']; zm = A['zmid']
    St.box((-0.012, 0, zm - 0.02), (0.026, A['w'] + 0.006, 0.14), 'dark', 0.006)
    St.prism([(0.02, 0.06), (0.16, 0.06), (0.2, 0.074), (0.02, 0.074)], A['w'] - 0.008, 'furniture', 0.004); A['stock_len'] = 0.0
def stock_none(P, S, A):
    P['stock'].cyl((-0.006, 0, 0), 0.02, 0.012, 'body', seg=12); A['stock_len'] = 0.0
STOCK = {'fixed_wood': stock_wood, 'fixed_poly': stock_poly, 'folding_wire': stock_wire, 'folding_strut': stock_strut, 'bullpup_integral': stock_bullpup, 'none': stock_none}

# ---------------- HANDGUARDS ----------------
def hg_wood(P, S, A):
    H = P['handguard']; x = A['hg_x0']; Lh = g(S, 'length', 0.27)
    H.cyl((x + Lh * 0.315, 0, 0.028), 0.0215, Lh * 0.63, 'furniture', seg=18)
    H.box((x + Lh / 2, 0, -0.014), (Lh, 0.046, 0.052), 'furniture', 0.008)
    for k in range(4): H.box((x + 0.045 + k * 0.045 * Lh / 0.27, 0, -0.042), (0.012, 0.05, 0.006), 'barrel', 0.0015)
    A.update(hg_x1=x + Lh, hg_w=0.025, hg_zmid=-0.014, hg_covers_gas=True)
def hg_quad(P, S, A):
    H = P['handguard']; x = A['hg_x0']; Lh = g(S, 'length', 0.26); r = 0.0255
    H.cyl((x + Lh / 2, 0, 0), r, Lh, 'body', seg=16)
    for ang in range(4):
        a = ang * math.pi / 2; cy, cz = math.sin(a) * (r + 0.003), math.cos(a) * (r + 0.003)
        wy, wz = (0.018, 0.006) if ang % 2 == 0 else (0.006, 0.018)
        H.box((x + Lh / 2, cy, cz), (Lh, wy, wz), 'barrel')
        for i in range(int(Lh / 0.022)):
            H.box((x + 0.011 + i * 0.022, cy * 1.0 + math.sin(a) * 0.004, cz + math.cos(a) * 0.004), (0.011, wy, wz) if ang % 2 == 0 else (0.011, wy, wz), 'barrel')
    A.update(hg_x1=x + Lh, hg_w=r + 0.006, hg_zmid=0.0, hg_covers_gas=False)
def hg_slim(P, S, A):
    H = P['handguard']; x = A['hg_x0']; Lh = g(S, 'length', 0.24)
    pts = [(-0.021, 0.024), (0.021, 0.024), (0.030, 0.002), (0.024, -0.026), (-0.024, -0.026), (-0.030, 0.002)]
    H.prism(pts, Lh, g(S, 'material', 'furniture'), 0.003, plane='yz', c=x)
    for i in range(int(Lh / 0.045) - 1):
        for s in (-1, 1): H.box((x + 0.04 + i * 0.045, s * 0.0292, 0.002), (0.022, 0.002, 0.012), 'dark')
    A.update(hg_x1=x + Lh, hg_w=0.03, hg_zmid=0.002, hg_covers_gas=False)
def hg_shroud(P, S, A):
    H = P['handguard']; x = A['hg_x0']; Lh = g(S, 'length', 0.20); r = 0.024
    H.cyl((x + Lh / 2, 0, 0), r, Lh, 'body', seg=16)
    for i in range(int(Lh / 0.022)): H.cyl((x + 0.012 + i * 0.022, 0, 0), r + 0.0025, 0.006, 'barrel', seg=16)
    A.update(hg_x1=x + Lh, hg_w=r + 0.003, hg_zmid=0.0, hg_covers_gas=False)
def hg_none(P, S, A): A.update(hg_x1=A['x1'], hg_w=0.02, hg_zmid=0.0, hg_covers_gas=False)
HAND = {'wood_ak': hg_wood, 'rail_quad': hg_quad, 'slim_poly': hg_slim, 'ribbed_shroud': hg_shroud, 'none': hg_none}

# ---------------- BARREL + MUZZLE + GAS ----------------
def barrel(P, S, A, gas):
    B = P['barrel']; Lb = g(S, 'length', 0.42); r = g(S, 'radius', 0.0115); prof = g(S, 'profile', 'plain'); bx = A['x1'] - 0.01; mx = A['x1'] + Lb
    xc = (bx + mx) / 2; ln = mx - bx
    if prof == 'tapered': B.cyl((xc, 0, 0), r * 1.6, ln, 'barrel', r2=r, seg=16)
    elif prof == 'heavy': B.cyl((xc, 0, 0), r * 1.4, ln, 'barrel', seg=16)
    elif prof == 'shrouded':
        B.cyl((xc, 0, 0), r, ln, 'barrel', seg=16); B.cyl((bx + ln * 0.33, 0, 0), r * 2.3, ln * 0.66, 'body', seg=16, bevel=0.003)
    else: B.cyl((xc, 0, 0), r, ln, 'barrel', seg=16)
    mz = g(S, 'muzzle', 'brake'); A['muzzle_x'] = mx
    if mz == 'brake':
        B.cyl((mx + 0.025, 0, 0), r * 1.3, 0.05, 'barrel', seg=16, bevel=0.002)
        for dx in (0.015, 0.03): B.cyl((mx + dx, 0, 0), r * 1.32, 0.004, 'dark', seg=16)
    elif mz == 'flash_hider':
        B.cyl((mx + 0.03, 0, 0), r * 1.35, 0.06, 'barrel', r2=r * 1.1, seg=12)
        B.box((mx + 0.045, 0, 0), (0.028, r * 3.0, 0.003), 'dark'); B.box((mx + 0.045, 0, 0), (0.028, 0.003, r * 3.0), 'dark')
    elif mz == 'suppressor':
        sl = g(S, 'suppressor_length', 0.17); B.cyl((mx - 0.01 + sl / 2, 0, 0), r * 3.0, sl, 'body', seg=18, bevel=0.003)
        B.cyl((mx - 0.01 + sl + 0.002, 0, 0), r * 3.05, 0.004, 'dark', seg=18)
    else: B.cyl((mx + 0.006, 0, 0), r * 1.15, 0.012, 'barrel', seg=14)
    if gas:
        gx = mx - min(0.13, Lb * 0.35); z = r + 0.0225; x_s = A['hg_x1'] - (0.03 if A.get('hg_covers_gas') else 0.005)
        B.box((gx, 0, 0.014), (0.04, 0.03, 0.056), 'barrel', 0.005)
        B.rod((min(x_s, gx - 0.05), 0, z), (gx + 0.02, 0, z), 0.0135, 'barrel', seg=14)
    A['gas'] = gas

# ---------------- SIGHTS ----------------
def sights(P, S, A, r):
    Sg = P['sights']; fr = g(S, 'front', 'post'); rr = g(S, 'rear', 'tangent'); xf = A['muzzle_x'] - 0.065; zt = r + 0.022
    if fr in ('post', 'hooded'):
        Sg.box((xf, 0, 0.011), (0.026, 0.016, r * 2 + 0.022), 'barrel', 0.003)
        Sg.box((xf, 0, zt + 0.009), (0.004, 0.004, 0.02), 'barrel')
        if fr == 'hooded':
            for s in (-1, 1): Sg.box((xf, s * 0.0085, zt + 0.012), (0.016, 0.003, 0.03), 'barrel', 0.001)
    x, z = A['sight_x'], A['z_top']
    if rr == 'tangent':
        Sg.box((x, 0, z + 0.008), (0.03, 0.02, 0.016), 'barrel', 0.003); Sg.box((x + 0.015, 0, z + 0.019), (0.004, 0.014, 0.012), 'barrel')
    elif rr == 'notch':
        Sg.box((x, 0, z + 0.005), (0.024, 0.02, 0.01), 'barrel', 0.002)
        for s in (-1, 1): Sg.box((x, s * 0.007, z + 0.014), (0.012, 0.004, 0.018), 'barrel', 0.001)
    elif rr == 'carry_handle':
        for dx in (-0.045, 0.045): Sg.box((x + dx, 0, z + 0.02), (0.014, 0.02, 0.04), 'body', 0.003)
        Sg.box((x, 0, z + 0.046), (0.11, 0.024, 0.012), 'body', 0.004); Sg.box((x - 0.04, 0, z + 0.055), (0.006, 0.012, 0.008), 'dark')
    elif rr == 'red_dot':
        Sg.box((x, 0, z + 0.006), (0.05, 0.03, 0.012), 'body', 0.002); Sg.box((x, 0, z + 0.034), (0.056, 0.034, 0.044), 'body', 0.005)
        for s in (-1, 1): Sg.box((x + s * 0.0285, 0, z + 0.036), (0.002, 0.026, 0.032), 'accent')
    A['sight_top'] = z
# Sci-fi supply crate r3 (darker lid, saturated glow, lid ribs, join by material), 1.0 x 0.6 x 0.6 m, Z up, base on z=0
L, W, H = 1.0, 0.6, 0.6
foot = 0.05
hull = mat('hull', (0.05, 0.08, 0.07), 0.6, 0.5)
frame = mat('frame', (0.03, 0.035, 0.04), 0.9, 0.35)
panel = mat('panel', (0.10, 0.15, 0.13), 0.5, 0.45)
accent = mat('accent', (0.85, 0.55, 0.02), 0.2, 0.5)
glow = mat('glow', (0.0, 0.35, 1.0), 0.0, 0.3, emit=(0.0, 0.45, 1.0))
zc = foot + (H - foot) / 2
bh = H - foot
box('body', (0, 0, zc), (L, W, bh), hull, 0.012)
t = 0.04
for sx in (-1, 1):
    for sy in (-1, 1):
        box('post', (sx * (L / 2 - t / 2 + 0.004), sy * (W / 2 - t / 2 + 0.004), zc), (t + 0.008, t + 0.008, bh), frame, 0.01)
        # chunky corner caps top and bottom
        for z in (foot + 0.045, H - 0.045):
            box('cap', (sx * (L / 2 - 0.045), sy * (W / 2 - 0.045), z), (0.1, 0.1, 0.09), frame, 0.015)
# belt seam under lid
box('seam', (0, 0, H - 0.115), (L + 0.012, W + 0.012, 0.016), frame, 0.004)
box('lid', (0, 0, H + 0.012), (L - 0.04, W - 0.04, 0.035), frame, 0.008)
box('lid_inset', (0, 0, H + 0.032), (L - 0.2, W - 0.2, 0.012), hull, 0.004)
for sx in (-1, 1):
    box('lid_rib', (sx * 0.3, 0, H + 0.042), (0.03, W - 0.26, 0.012), frame, 0.004)
# long-face panels: raised plate + 3 ribs + inset
for sy in (-1, 1):
    for sx in (-1, 1):
        px = sx * 0.235
        box('panel', (px, sy * (W / 2 + 0.006), zc - 0.03), (0.38, 0.014, bh - 0.26), panel, 0.006)
        for k in (-1, 0, 1):
            box('rib', (px, sy * (W / 2 + 0.016), zc - 0.03 + k * 0.09), (0.32, 0.012, 0.025), hull, 0.004)
# yellow label plate + warning bar on each long face center
for sy in (-1, 1):
    box('label', (0, sy * (W / 2 + 0.01), zc - 0.03), (0.13, 0.012, 0.16), accent, 0.004)
    for k in (-1, 1):
        box('labbar', (0, sy * (W / 2 + 0.017), zc - 0.03 + k * 0.045), (0.09, 0.006, 0.02), frame, 0.002)
# glowing status strip on the front, in FRONT of panel, plus lid-side light
box('glow', (0.0, -(W / 2 + 0.03), zc - 0.17), (0.26, 0.006, 0.018), glow, 0.0)
box('glow2', (0.0, (W / 2 + 0.03), zc - 0.17), (0.26, 0.006, 0.018), glow, 0.0)
# end faces: panel + upper carry handles
for sx in (-1, 1):
    box('endpanel', (sx * (L / 2 + 0.006), 0, zc - 0.03), (0.014, W - 0.2, bh - 0.26), panel, 0.006)
    box('endrib', (sx * (L / 2 + 0.016), 0, zc - 0.1), (0.012, 0.3, 0.025), hull, 0.004)
    hz = zc + 0.1
    box('h_bar', (sx * (L / 2 + 0.055), 0, hz), (0.03, 0.26, 0.03), frame, 0.01)
    for sy in (-1, 1):
        box('h_post', (sx * (L / 2 + 0.028), sy * 0.115, hz), (0.056, 0.03, 0.03), frame, 0.008)
# big latches (2 per long side)
for sy in (-1, 1):
    for sx in (-1, 1):
        box('latch', (sx * 0.4, sy * (W / 2 + 0.022), H - 0.14), (0.07, 0.03, 0.12), frame, 0.01)
        box('latch_pin', (sx * 0.4, sy * (W / 2 + 0.042), H - 0.12), (0.03, 0.012, 0.03), accent, 0.004)
for sx in (-1, 1):
    for sy in (-1, 1):
        box('foot', (sx * (L / 2 - 0.07), sy * (W / 2 - 0.07), foot / 2), (0.12, 0.12, foot), frame, 0.008)
